title: Deep-learning virtual screening finds antibacterial hits in over one billion compounds
summary: Genentech and collaborators trained the deep-learning model GNEprop on high-throughput screening data and screened more than 1.4 billion synthetically accessible molecules. In follow-up experiments, 82 selected compounds showed antibacterial activity against the sensitized E. coli ΔtolC strain; the paper reports a 90-fold higher hit rate than the training screen and describes chemically diverse hits, some with activity beyond that strain and validated biological targets.
organization: Genentech Research and Early Development; NVIDIA; Mila–Université de Montréal collaborators

evidence.tested: In follow-up experiments, 82 selected compounds showed antibacterial activity against the sensitized E. coli ΔtolC strain; the paper reports a 90-fold higher hit rate than the training screen and describes chemically diverse hits, some with activity beyond that strain and validated biological targets.
evidence.unknown: The 82 confirmed hits were tested for single-dose activity against the sensitized E. coli ΔtolC screening strain; this is not evidence that all 82 work against wild-type bacteria or in infections. The 90-fold improvement refers to hit rate relative to the HTS training experiment. Some additional compounds were selected for dose-response testing; do not imply all virtual hits were validated. A publisher correction fixed a coauthor’s misspelled first name and did not change results.
evidence.ai_role: GNEprop was trained on approximately two million small molecules screened against E. coli ΔtolC and used to rank a much larger synthetically accessible library for experimental prioritization. The follow-up assays confirmed antibacterial activity for 82 compounds; biological characterization also investigated specific targets.
